diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says RAIN, datasheet reading says RJ11 centre conductor 1
diffs.evidence: Both readings describe the same wire: the datasheet says the 'switch is connected to the two center conductors of the attached RJ' 11 cable, and the part's pin 1 RAIN is one of those centre conductors (the GPIO side of the non-polarised reed switch), just given a functional name instead of 'conductor 1'.

diffs.diff: header pin 2: part says GND, datasheet reading says RJ11 centre conductor 2
diffs.evidence: The datasheet says 'These sensors contain no active electronics, instead using sealed magnetic' reed switches, so the second centre conductor is simply the other switch lead; the part names it GND because that is where it is wired (switch not polarised), which is equivalent to 'RJ11 centre conductor 2'.

diffs.diff: rainfall_mm: datasheet reading gives 0.2794 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: The datasheet states 'Each 0.2794mm of rain cause one' momentary contact closure, and the part already uses exactly that constant (driver MM_PER_TIP = 0.2794, example test expects 3 tips = 0.8382 mm); the gate sees none only because a passive switch is simulated as a one-key keypad-matrix, which has no measure/scale field.
